messages.body_plain: Hi team, I want reproduce a tree in  Wu, Linwei, et al. "Reduction of microbial diversity in grassland soil is driven by long-term climate warming." Nature Microbiology (2022): 1-9.  doi:10.1038/s41564-022-01147-3. using ggtree. However, I cannot produce this layout using ggtree or other softwares (e.g. iTOL). Can anyone give me some advice？

messages.subject: Re: Anyone knows how to get this layout?
messages.subject_clean: Anyone knows how to get this layout?
messages.body_plain:
If you are talking about the tree layout, it should be:

ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none", layout = "slanted") + layout_circular()

messages.subject: Changing the axis after view clade
messages.subject_clean: Changing the axis after view clade
messages.body_plain:
I have a tree, and viewclade works on this tree, but I want to change the x-axis to make the branch lengths easier to see. This is likely in the documentation, but I couldn't find it.

Current code
```
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtree)
library(treeio)

tree <- read.newick(paste("/Volumes/ARLN/CRAB/grandeur/iqtree2/iqtree.treefile", sep = ""))

test <- ggtree(tree, size = 0.25) +
  geom_tiplab(color="black", size=3) +
  theme_tree2()

viewClade(test, 47)
```

I want to change the axis to go from something like 0.0088 to 0.0092, but something like adding ggplot2::xlim(0, 0.0092) did not work.

messages.subject: Scaling branch width by support (or other parameters)
messages.subject_clean: Scaling branch width by support (or other parameters)
messages.body_plain:
Hello all:

I've gotten into the habit of using branch width to show clade support in my tree figures but typically do this manually. It recently occurred to me that there could be a way to do this programmatically in ggtree but I have been unable to figure it out on my own.

What I want to do is specify a branch/line width using the "support" parameter of the tree as a threshold. For example, all branches with support >= 0.7 will have width = 4 while all branches with support < 0.7 have width = 2. Is this possible?

Cheers,

Kurt Wollenberg, Ph.D.

Contractor - MSC, Inc. | A Guidehouse Company
Phylogenetics Specialist
Scientific Support Section
Bioinformatics and Computational Biosciences Branch (BCBB)
OCICB/OSMO/OD/NIAID/NIH
